title: Peter defends the Gentile mission + Antioch, where the disciples are first called Christians

paragraphs.text: Now the apostles and the brethren that were in Judaea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
paragraphs.original: Ἤκουσαν δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ οἱ ὄντες κατὰ τὴν Ἰουδαίαν ὅτι καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousan de hoi apostoloi kai hoi adelphoi hoi ontes kata tēn Ioudaian hoti kai ta ethnē edexanto ton logon tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβη Πέτρος εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, διεκρίνοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς
paragraphs.translit: hote de anebē Petros eis Ierousalēm, diekrinonto pros auton hoi ek peritomēs

paragraphs.text: saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.
paragraphs.original: λέγοντες ὅτι Εἰσῆλθες πρὸς ἄνδρας ἀκροβυστίαν ἔχοντας καὶ συνέφαγες αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: legontes hoti Eisēlthes pros andras akrobystian echontas kai synephages autois.

paragraphs.text: But Peter began, and expounded [the matter] unto them in order, saying,
paragraphs.original: ἀρξάμενος δὲ Πέτρος ἐξετίθετο αὐτοῖς καθεξῆς λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: arxamenos de Petros exetitheto autois kathexēs legōn·

paragraphs.text: I was in the city of Joppa praying: and in a trance I saw a vision, a certain vessel descending, as it were a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even unto me:
paragraphs.original: Ἐγὼ ἤμην ἐν πόλει Ἰόππῃ προσευχόμενος καὶ εἶδον ἐν ἐκστάσει ὅραμα, καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιεμένην ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἦλθεν ἄχρι ἐμοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Egō ēmēn en polei Ioppē proseuchomenos kai eidon en ekstasei horama, katabainon skeuos ti hōs othonēn megalēn tessarsin archais kathiemenēn ek tou ouranou, kai ēlthen achri emou·

paragraphs.text: upon which when I had fastened mine eyes, I considered, and saw the fourfooted beasts of the earth and wild beasts and creeping things and birds of the heaven.
paragraphs.original: εἰς ἣν ἀτενίσας κατενόουν καὶ εἶδον τὰ τετράποδα τῆς γῆς καὶ τὰ θηρία καὶ τὰ ἑρπετὰ καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: eis hēn atenisas katenooun kai eidon ta tetrapoda tēs gēs kai ta thēria kai ta herpeta kai ta peteina tou ouranou·

paragraphs.text: And I heard also a voice saying unto me, Rise, Peter; kill and eat.
paragraphs.original: ἤκουσα δὲ καὶ φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι· Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.
paragraphs.translit: ēkousa de kai phōnēs legousēs moi· Anastas, Petre, thyson kai phage.

paragraphs.text: But I said, Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath ever entered into my mouth.
paragraphs.original: εἶπον δέ· Μηδαμῶς, κύριε, ὅτι κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον οὐδέποτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ στόμα μου.
paragraphs.translit: eipon de· Mēdamōs, kyrie, hoti koinon ē akatharton oudepote eisēlthen eis to stoma mou.

paragraphs.text: But a voice answered the second time out of heaven, What God hath cleansed, make not thou common.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ φωνὴ ἐκ δευτέρου ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ· Ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē de phōnē ek deuterou ek tou ouranou· Ha ho theos ekatharisen sy mē koinou.

paragraphs.text: And this was done thrice: and all were drawn up again into heaven.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ ἀνεσπάσθη πάλιν ἅπαντα εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
paragraphs.translit: touto de egeneto epi tris, kai anespasthē palin hapanta eis ton ouranon.

paragraphs.text: And behold, forthwith three men stood before the house in which we were, having been sent from Caesarea unto me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξαυτῆς τρεῖς ἄνδρες ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐν ᾗ ἦμεν, ἀπεσταλμένοι ἀπὸ Καισαρείας πρός με.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou exautēs treis andres epestēsan epi tēn oikian en hē ēmen, apestalmenoi apo Kaisareias pros me.

paragraphs.text: And the Spirit bade me go with them, making no distinction. And these six brethren also accompanied me; and we entered into the man`s house:
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμά μοι συνελθεῖν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρίναντα. ἦλθον δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ καὶ οἱ ἓξ ἀδελφοὶ οὗτοι, καὶ εἰσήλθομεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀνδρός.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de to pneuma moi synelthein autois mēden diakrinanta. ēlthon de syn emoi kai hoi hex adelphoi houtoi, kai eisēlthomen eis ton oikon tou andros.

paragraphs.text: and he told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house, and saying, Send to Joppa, and fetch Simon, whose surname is Peter;
paragraphs.original: ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ἡμῖν πῶς εἶδεν τὸν ἄγγελον ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ σταθέντα καὶ εἰπόντα· Ἀπόστειλον εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνα τὸν ἐπικαλούμενον Πέτρον,
paragraphs.translit: apēngeilen de hēmin pōs eiden ton angelon en tō oikō autou stathenta kai eiponta· Aposteilon eis Ioppēn kai metapempsai Simōna ton epikaloumenon Petron,

paragraphs.text: who shall speak unto thee words, whereby thou shalt be saved, thou and all thy house.
paragraphs.original: ὃς λαλήσει ῥήματα πρὸς σὲ ἐν οἷς σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ πᾶς ὁ οἶκός σου.
paragraphs.translit: hos lalēsei rhēmata pros se en hois sōthēsē sy kai pas ho oikos sou.

paragraphs.text: And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.
paragraphs.original: ἐν δὲ τῷ ἄρξασθαί με λαλεῖν ἐπέπεσεν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ὥσπερ καὶ ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀρχῇ.
paragraphs.translit: en de tō arxasthai me lalein epepesen to pneuma to hagion epʼ autous hōsper kai ephʼ hēmas en archē.

paragraphs.text: And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.original: ἐμνήσθην δὲ τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ κυρίου ὡς ἔλεγεν· Ἰωάννης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ βαπτισθήσεσθε ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.
paragraphs.translit: emnēsthēn de tou rhēmatos tou kyriou hōs elegen· Iōannēs men ebaptisen hydati, hymeis de baptisthēsesthe en pneumati hagiō.

paragraphs.text: If then God gave unto them the like gift as [he did] also unto us, when we believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?
paragraphs.original: εἰ οὖν τὴν ἴσην δωρεὰν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς ὡς καὶ ἡμῖν πιστεύσασιν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ἐγὼ τίς ἤμην δυνατὸς κωλῦσαι τὸν θεόν;
paragraphs.translit: ei oun tēn isēn dōrean edōken autois ho theos hōs kai hēmin pisteusasin epi ton kyrion Iēsoun Christon, egō tis ēmēn dynatos kōlysai ton theon;

paragraphs.text: And when they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then to the Gentiles also hath God granted repentance unto life.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ταῦτα ἡσύχασαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες· Ἄρα καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὁ θεὸς τὴν μετάνοιαν εἰς ζωὴν ἔδωκεν.
paragraphs.translit: akousantes de tauta hēsychasan kai edoxasan ton theon legontes· Ara kai tois ethnesin ho theos tēn metanoian eis zōēn edōken.

paragraphs.text: They therefore that were scattered abroad upon the tribulation that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phoenicia, and Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to none save only to Jews.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες ἀπὸ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς γενομένης ἐπὶ Στεφάνῳ διῆλθον ἕως Φοινίκης καὶ Κύπρου καὶ Ἀντιοχείας μηδενὶ λαλοῦντες τὸν λόγον εἰ μὴ μόνον Ἰουδαίοις.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi men oun diasparentes apo tēs thlipseōs tēs genomenēs epi Stephanō diēlthon heōs Phoinikēs kai Kyprou kai Antiocheias mēdeni lalountes ton logon ei mē monon Ioudaiois.

paragraphs.text: But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Greeks also, preaching the Lord Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δέ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες Κύπριοι καὶ Κυρηναῖοι, οἵτινες ἐλθόντες εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ἐλάλουν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de tines ex autōn andres Kyprioi kai Kyrēnaioi, hoitines elthontes eis Antiocheian elaloun kai pros tous Hellēnistas, euangelizomenoi ton kyrion Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number that believed turned unto the Lord.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦν χεὶρ κυρίου μετʼ αὐτῶν, πολύς τε ἀριθμὸς ὁ πιστεύσας ἐπέστρεψεν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēn cheir kyriou metʼ autōn, polys te arithmos ho pisteusas epestrepsen epi ton kyrion.

paragraphs.text: And the report concerning them came to the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas as far as Antioch:
paragraphs.original: ἠκούσθη δὲ ὁ λόγος εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς οὔσης ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ περὶ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν Βαρναβᾶν ἕως Ἀντιοχείας·
paragraphs.translit: ēkousthē de ho logos eis ta ōta tēs ekklēsias tēs ousēs en Ierousalēm peri autōn, kai exapesteilan Barnaban heōs Antiocheias·

paragraphs.text: who, when he was come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad; and he exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord:
paragraphs.original: ὃς παραγενόμενος καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν χάριν τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐχάρη καὶ παρεκάλει πάντας τῇ προθέσει τῆς καρδίας προσμένειν τῷ κυρίῳ,
paragraphs.translit: hos paragenomenos kai idōn tēn charin tēn tou theou, echarē kai parekalei pantas tē prothesei tēs kardias prosmenein tō kyriō,

paragraphs.text: for he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἦν ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου καὶ πίστεως. καὶ προσετέθη ὄχλος ἱκανὸς τῷ κυρίῳ.
paragraphs.translit: hoti ēn anēr agathos kai plērēs pneumatos hagiou kai pisteōs. kai prosetethē ochlos hikanos tō kyriō.

paragraphs.text: And he went forth to Tarsus to seek for Saul;
paragraphs.original: ἐξῆλθεν δὲ εἰς Ταρσὸν ἀναζητῆσαι Σαῦλον,
paragraphs.translit: exēlthen de eis Tarson anazētēsai Saulon,

paragraphs.text: and when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that even for a whole year they were gathered together with the church, and taught much people, and that the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὑρὼν ἤγαγεν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν. ἐγένετο δὲ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ὅλον συναχθῆναι ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ καὶ διδάξαι ὄχλον ἱκανόν, χρηματίσαι τε πρώτως ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τοὺς μαθητὰς Χριστιανούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai heurōn ēgagen eis Antiocheian. egeneto de autois kai eniauton holon synachthēnai en tē ekklēsia kai didaxai ochlon hikanon, chrēmatisai te prōtōs en Antiocheia tous mathētas Christianous.

paragraphs.text: Now in these days there came down prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν ταύταις δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις κατῆλθον ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων προφῆται εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν·
paragraphs.translit: En tautais de tais hēmerais katēlthon apo Hierosolymōn prophētai eis Antiocheian·

paragraphs.text: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be a great famine over all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius.
paragraphs.original: ἀναστὰς δὲ εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος ἐσήμανεν διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος λιμὸν μεγάλην μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν οἰκουμένην· ἥτις ἐγένετο ἐπὶ Κλαυδίου.
paragraphs.translit: anastas de heis ex autōn onomati Hagabos esēmanen dia tou pneumatos limon megalēn mellein esesthai ephʼ holēn tēn oikoumenēn· hētis egeneto epi Klaudiou.

paragraphs.text: And the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren that dwelt in Judea:
paragraphs.original: τῶν δὲ μαθητῶν καθὼς εὐπορεῖτό τις ὥρισαν ἕκαστος αὐτῶν εἰς διακονίαν πέμψαι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ ἀδελφοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: tōn de mathētōn kathōs euporeito tis hōrisan hekastos autōn eis diakonian pempsai tois katoikousin en tē Ioudaia adelphois·

paragraphs.text: which also they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
paragraphs.original: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησαν ἀποστείλαντες πρὸς τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους διὰ χειρὸς Βαρναβᾶ καὶ Σαύλου.
paragraphs.translit: ho kai epoiēsan aposteilantes pros tous presbyterous dia cheiros Barnaba kai Saulou.
